tools.name: run_create
tools.title: Create dossier
tools.description: Create an owned dossier when you need tracked claims, evidence with sources, coverage or audit. For a single exact check prefer calculate/solve_math/solve_logic instead. Restricted runs stay within server storage. profile picks an operator-approved budget envelope (standard by default; larger envelopes are bounded by the operator policy). For anonymous access the reply embeds a one-time dossier capability in the returned identifier: keep it exactly as returned — it authorizes every later operation on this dossier and is never re-issued.

goal.description: What this dossier must establish, in one free-text goal. The host formalizes it later; the server never invents claims or proof inputs.

externalAllowed.description: true allows sending the necessary content to external processors (Jev, web search); false keeps everything server-side except the exact kernel.

tools.name: calculate
tools.title: Calculate (exact)
tools.description: Exact arithmetic without floating-point truth claims. Grammar: rationals, factorial(n), binomial(n,k), gcd, lcm, mod(a,m), powmod(a,e,m), n!, `a mod b`, and ONE top-level comparison (=, !=, <, <=, >, >=). Pure operation: no dossier, no audit record. tools.name: finite_compute
tools.title: Finite computation
tools.description: Bounded declarative computation: range_reduce (sum/product/count over an inclusive integer range; optional modulus), linear_recurrence (a_n = c0*a_(n-1) + c1*a_(n-2) + ..., coefficients listed most recent first; optional modulus), bounded_search (exhaustive enumeration of a bounded integer space against one comparison predicate). Declarative only: no clock, network, files or dynamic code; a reached limit returns a partial result, never a fake maximum or absence.

operation.description: Declarative operation; see the tool description for the exact recipe of each.

expression.description: Expression over the declared variable(s); for bounded_search this is part of the predicate.

to.description: Inclusive integer upper bound, as an exact integer literal.

modulus.description: Optional positive modulus applied to the result.

initial.description: Initial terms in chronological order: a_0, a_1, ... (linear_recurrence).

variables.description: Variable names used by the predicate.

predicate.description: Comparison predicate for bounded_search: expression + its variable names.

ranges.description: Search space per variable, inclusive ranges (bounded_search).

maxResults.description: Cap on returned matches; a reached limit returns a partial result, never a fake maximum.

tools.name: cas
tools.title: Symbolic CAS (isolated worker)
tools.description: Isolated symbolic recipes: identity (expression equal to rhs?), simplify, solve (ONE symbol, univariate polynomial, rational coefficients, degree <= 8, exact roots including multiplicities). Runs only in the separate IAM-protected worker with pinned image; no arbitrary Python and no local fallback. A library result is not proof-kernel certification. assumptions is optional, e.g. "t=real, u=positive". Domain assumptions are applied: roots excluded by the declared domain are reported in excludedRoots and never counted as solutions. The worker bounds are published in capabilities.scientific (expression <= 2000 bytes, <= 8 symbols).

operation.description: identity: is expression equal to rhs? simplify: reduce expression. solve: exact roots of a univariate polynomial (degree <= 8).

expression.description: Exact symbolic expression (e.g. "sqrt(x^2)", "x^2 - 3*x + 2"); at most 2000 UTF-8 bytes.

rhs.description: Right-hand side for identity checks; at most 2000 UTF-8 bytes.

symbols.description: Free variable names (max 8); required by the recipe for most expressions.

assumptions.description: Optional domain assumptions as text, e.g. "x=real, y=positive" (domains: real, positive, integer, nonzero, complex); at most 8 entries.

requestKey.description: Optional idempotency key (<=100 chars); when omitted a stable key is derived, so an identical retry is never re-executed.
